lar-uri.comment: A lar: URI reads as an address wherever it stands, sigil or prose. TW5 binds no rule to the scheme, so the base grammar takes its '//' for an italic run. RULED 2026-10-06 (lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/api/pono.uri-palette, the punctuation-and-no-underline pass): a lar: address NAMES rather than fetches, so the whole family wears a COLOURLESS parent — `meta.uri.lar.memetic-wikitext`, measured 0/65 bundled themes give it any foreground or fontStyle of its own — and every separator (the scheme's own ':'/'://, the slash introducing the root, every other path slash, the authority's ':'/'@') reads as plain punctuation with nothing to override it. Each NAMED leaf (persona, role, place, heading, angle, dynamic) still carries its own distinguishing scope and so keeps its own ink. RULED 2026-10-06 (path text gets a name themes paint): arbitrary path text — any segment past the heading.angle.dynamic root — now wears `variable.other.constant.path.lar.memetic-wikitext` rather than a colourless wrapper, reaching 65/65 themes while staying a distinct family from the root triad's own leaves (see that scope's own comment below). Only '=' names a parameter. RULED 2026-10-07 (the operator's eyes-on pass): the role wears `entity.name.role.lar.memetic-wikitext`, not `support.role…`. The old name reached 23 of 65 bundled themes, through the bare `support` prefix alone, so a role read as fallback text beside two siblings that paint — persona and place both reach 40 of 65 under `entity.name`, and the role now reaches the same 40, so the authority's three parts paint together or not at all. RULED 2026-10-08 (the texture pass, REVERSING the 2026-10-06 colourless-separator ruling for the lar: and ni: families specifically — the base grammar's own fused `https://`-style run stays as ruled, see LEDGER-3.0.0.md): the operator read both grammars in the editor and found an underline reads as one continuous stroke, broken wherever a punctuation ink interrupts it — but this dialect's addresses carry NO underline (ruled days earlier), so breaking the stroke costs nothing, and the operator wants the texture a broken run gives instead. Two moves, both measured below with `tools/uri-span-measure.js` / `tools/uri-span-compare.js` and `tools/theme-model.js` `styleOf` over all 65 bundled themes: (1) a SCHEME run paints as one colour — the separator ('`:`'/'`://`') stacks the SAME scheme family the scheme word already carries, the way the base's own `https://` does, so `lar:` and `lar://` (and `ni:`/`ni:///`) read as one unbroken scheme ink; (2) every INTERIOR separator takes the colour of the segment it opens rather than reading as plain punctuation — the slash before the root takes the heading's ink, each root dot takes the ink of the leaf that follows it, every other path slash takes the path text's own two-level ink, the authority's ':' takes the role's ink and its '@' takes the place's ink. The punctuation scope name is kept as the OUTER/ancestor name in every stack — selectors and the house vocabulary that key on it still reach it — while the segment family rides INNERMOST, where the house's measured fallback-chain law (RE-PRICED 2026-10-07, see capture 5 below) says the innermost name a theme reaches wins the colour.
lar-uri.name: meta.uri.lar.memetic-wikitext
lar-uri.endComment: RULED 2026-10-08 (the operator's SECOND eyes-on pass): a quoted query value opens on the same quote character this `end` pattern watches for, so without this flag the region closed BEFORE the new quoted-value pattern (in `patterns` below) ever got a turn, and `?form="quoted"` read as plain paragraph text past the `=` — not even a 'string' ancestor, nothing at all. `applyEndPatternLast` tries every nested pattern FIRST at a tied position and falls back to `end` only if none claims it; checked against every OTHER character this `end` matches (plain space, '>', ']', an unpaired quote with no preceding '='), no pattern in this rule's `patterns` list can start a match there, so the region still closes exactly where it did before everywhere except the one case this exists to fix.

1.comment: RULED 2026-10-08 (the operator's SECOND eyes-on pass, parting the scheme run from the authority): measured with tools/theme-model.js styleOf, `support.type.scheme.lar` alone shares its resolved colour with the bare `entity.name` the persona/role/place leaves fall back to in 18 of 65 themes — Gruvbox (all six variants), horizon/horizon-bright, kanagawa (dragon/lotus/wave), material-theme (all five variants), synthwave-84 and vesper — because those themes paint one generic rule across BOTH `support.type` and `entity.name` (measured literal collision, e.g. Gruvbox's `#fabd2f` names both). Priced against moving the authority instead (stacking a companion onto persona/role/place): every companion tried that parted the scheme collision also regressed persona's existing distinctness from the root triad (2/65 to no fewer than 5/65), a REGRESSION the house forbids. Moving the SCHEME'S OWN family instead costs nothing measured: `support.constant.scheme.lar` added innermost drops the scheme/authority collision from 18/65 to 4/65 (the remaining 4 are material-theme variants where the scheme simply falls to the editor default rather than colliding with anything painted), while scheme's collision with the root triad IMPROVES (9/65 to 3/65) and with path text improves (21/65 to 8/65) — no pair measured regresses. `support.constant` stays inside the `support` family the scheme already wears (a URI scheme is a fixed, reserved identifier, same spirit as a language's `support.constant`), so it names nothing dishonest.
1.name: keyword.other.scheme.lar.memetic-wikitext support.type.scheme.lar.memetic-wikitext support.constant.scheme.lar.memetic-wikitext

2.comment: The whole scheme-separator run — '://' or the bare ':' — reads as ONE punctuation span, not just the colon. RULED 2026-10-08 (the texture pass, reversing the colourless-separator ruling for THIS dialect only — the base grammar's autolink keeps its fused run, see LEDGER-3.0.0.md): a scheme run paints as ONE colour, the way the base's own `https://` does, so the separator stacks the SAME scheme family the scheme word (capture 1) already carries, innermost, so it wins the colour while `punctuation.definition.scheme` survives as the outer name for selectors. RULED 2026-10-08 (second pass): carries capture 1's same `support.constant.scheme.lar` addition, for the same reason — see capture 1's comment.
2.name: punctuation.definition.scheme.lar.memetic-wikitext keyword.other.scheme.lar.memetic-wikitext support.type.scheme.lar.memetic-wikitext support.constant.scheme.lar.memetic-wikitext

3.name: meta.uri.authority.lar.memetic-wikitext
3.comment: RULED 2026-10-06 (a roleless authority reads as an authority): the seed's own session form (`#/lar-uri`) spells `alias:grant@host` — a role is the law's own shape — so a bare `persona@place` stands in TENSION with it, common in practice but not licensed there. Ruled anyway: the base's begin regex now admits EITHER shape, and this second alternative reuses the first one's EXISTING leaf names — persona, the authority separator, place — with no role capture at all, because none stands. No new scope name was needed for either half.

patterns.comment: The authority: a persona, the role it holds, and the place it stands. RULED 2026-10-08 (the texture pass): each separator takes the ink of the part that FOLLOWS it — the ':' opens the role, the '@' opens the place — so the joint reads, not the literal glyph.

The roleless authority: a persona and the place it stands, no role between them. RULED 2026-10-08 (the texture pass): the '@' opens the place, same as the roled alternative above, so it shares that alternative's exact stacked name.

4.comment: RULED 2026-10-08 (the texture pass, REVERSING the prior NARROW ruling for this dialect — the dialect wears no underline, so it takes texture instead; see LEDGER-3.0.0.md for the base grammar's own refusal of this same move): the '/' introducing the root segment takes the ink of the root it opens — the heading, the first leaf of the heading.angle.dynamic triad standing right after it.
4.name: punctuation.separator.root.intro.lar.memetic-wikitext entity.name.tag.heading.lar.memetic-wikitext

5.comment: Was `string.unquoted.uri.lar.memetic-wikitext` — a 'string' ancestor most themes colour, which left every OTHER path separator loud even though each already carried its own punctuation leaf name. Then `meta.uri.path.lar.memetic-wikitext`, colourless (0/65 themes) — honest about naming no construct, but costing arbitrary path text ANY selector at all. PRICED 2026-10-06: `variable.other.constant.path.lar.memetic-wikitext` reaches 65/65 (via `variable`/`variable.other.constant`/`variable.other`) while staying a distinct family from the root triad's `entity.name.tag.*` leaves below — `entity.name.tag.lar…` also reaches 65/65 but collapses that distinction, and a `string.unquoted…` name re-introduces the string ancestor the prior ruling removed. RE-PRICED 2026-10-07 (the operator's cascade reading, measured): a space-joined name reads as a FALLBACK CHAIN — the innermost name a theme reaches wins each property its own rule sets, and a theme reaching none of it keeps what the outer name resolved. So the wrapper stacks `entity.name.other.path.lar.memetic-wikitext` INSIDE `variable.other.constant.path.lar.memetic-wikitext`: painted-and-visible rises from 44/65 to 59/65 because the two names stand quiet in nearly disjoint theme sets, reached-and-invisible falls from 21/65 to 6/65 (clear of the house bar of 16, where the single name stood one above it), the root triad keeps its distinctness at 60/65, and the outer name remains an ancestor so the separators nested in it keep the quiet joint they read today (6/65, where either single-name swap cost it half). `entity.name.other` names a real entity leaf and never `.tag`, so it collides with no root term. Every '/' inside still reads the quiet way capture 4's does.
5.name: variable.other.constant.path.lar.memetic-wikitext entity.name.other.path.lar.memetic-wikitext
5.comment: RULED 2026-10-08 (the operator's SECOND eyes-on pass, in Kimbie Dark: `/ha.ka.ba/lares/docs/reading#/the-eye.lands` read as ALL ONE colour — the root triad, the path text AND the fragment fused). Kimbie Dark is not among the house's 65 bundled themes; five bundled themes reproduce the phenomenon by eye — one-light, red, solarized-dark, solarized-light, vesper — because they rule on the bare `entity.name` selector with no deeper distinction, the same mechanism as the scheme/authority collision above. MEASURED AND REFUSED: stacking `constant.other.path.lar` innermost drops path-vs-root-triad from 5/65 to 1/65 and path-vs-fragment the same, but `constant.other.checksum.ni` (ni:'s own pre-existing digest family, untouched by this pass) sits under the SAME `constant.other` ancestor — the fix that parts path from root/frag in the kin themes COLLIDES path with ni:'s digest instead, 8/65 to 45/65, a regression the house forbids outright (`ni:'s digest stays distinct from its algorithm` was the stated floor; this breaks path-against-digest instead, which was never asked to move). Every other real, currently-themed family swept (variable.*, support.*, keyword.*, markup.*, entity.other.*) either sits under an ancestor some OTHER segment already claims (same collision, different victim) or matches no bundled theme at all (a safe no-op that does not fix the finding). `string.regexp` alone measured clean on every bound, and is refused on principle — it is the SAME `string` ancestor the 2026-10-06 ruling removed from this family, for the same reason (a blanket theme rule would drown the separators beside it). This pass leaves path AS IT STOOD after the first eyes-on round; the Kimbie-kin fusion stands UNFIXED, reported rather than patched with a regression, pending either a new family for ni:'s digest (freeing `constant.other` for path) or the operator accepting the path-vs-digest cost explicitly.

patterns.comment: The root segment: heading, angle of approach, carried dynamic. No leading slash here — capture 4 already consumed it when the lookahead matched. RULED 2026-10-08 (the texture pass): each dot takes the ink of the leaf it opens — dot1 opens angle, dot2 opens dynamic — so the SAME existing punctuation name now splits into two stacked forms rather than reading identically; a theme ruling on the bare `punctuation.separator.root.lar` name alone still reaches both.

Any other path separator (including the leading slash of a lar: URI whose body does not open with a heading.angle.dynamic root, where capture 4 above did not fire). RULED 2026-10-08 (the texture pass): a path slash resolves to the SAME ink as the path text beside it, so it carries that text's exact stacked name — the two-level `variable.other.constant.path` / `entity.name.other.path` fallback chain, not just the inner leaf. (Second pass: path's wrapper above was NOT given a third companion — see its own comment — so this separator stays as the first pass left it.)
patterns.name: punctuation.separator.path.lar.memetic-wikitext variable.other.constant.path.lar.memetic-wikitext entity.name.other.path.lar.memetic-wikitext

patterns.comment: A quoted value — `?form="quoted"`, the corpus's own form (corpus/memetic/reading.in-prose.mem). RULED 2026-10-08 (the operator's SECOND eyes-on pass): before this rule, the lar-uri region's own `end` pattern stops at the opening quote (`(?=[\s>"'\]])`), so a quoted value fell OUT of the URI entirely and read as plain paragraph text — not even a 'string' ancestor, nothing at all. This pattern is tried before that `end` match consumes the quote, so it wins the position and the value stays INSIDE the URI. The quote marks and the text between them both wear `markup.other.value.lar.memetic-wikitext` — chosen BY MEASUREMENT, not the obvious `string.quoted...`, which the house already ruled out for this family (see capture 5's comment above: a 'string' ancestor lets a theme's blanket rule drown every separator beside it). Priced against half a dozen honest alternatives (variable/constant/entity.other/support families), every one that painted ANY colour in any of the 65 bundled themes also introduced a NEW non-default collision with an already-distinct pair (persona, the root triad, or ni's digest) that the house forbids regressing. `markup.other.value.lar` is the only candidate measured to introduce ZERO new non-default collisions anywhere — its cost, stated plainly: it paints 0 of 65 bundled themes (none of them rule on bare `markup.other`), so the value reads as the editor's own default ink everywhere today. A future pass that finds a family painting SOME themes without regressing a measured pair should take it over this one; this ruling prefers an honest, safe no-op to a dishonest or regressive paint.

A bare value claims everything up to the next separator. RULED 2026-10-08 (second pass): carries the SAME `markup.other.value.lar` the quoted form above now wears, innermost, so a reader meets ONE value family whether or not it is quoted — the pre-existing `string.unquoted.memetic-wikitext` name stays as the outer/ancestor name (nothing selecting on it loses reach), but no longer decides the colour.
patterns.name: string.unquoted.memetic-wikitext markup.other.value.lar.memetic-wikitext

patterns.comment: RULED 2026-10-08 (the operator's SECOND eyes-on pass): `?` opens the query's first key and `&` opens the next one, so both now stack the key's own ink (`#named-param`'s `entity.other.attribute-name.memetic-wikitext`) rather than reading as plain punctuation — the same interior-separator law as every other joint in this file, folded in now that the query itself is in scope.
patterns.name: punctuation.separator.query.memetic-wikitext entity.other.attribute-name.memetic-wikitext

fragment.comment: A fragment names an anchor. This corpus writes it with a leading slash and dots. RULED 2026-10-07 (the operator's eyes-on pass): the anchor carries NO underline — the no-underline ruling swept the lar: and ni: families and missed this shared rule, which went on painting the link cue these naming schemes no longer claim in the 37 of 65 bundled themes that rule on `markup.underline`. `entity.name.tag.anchor` reaches all 65 on its own, so the fragment keeps its ink without borrowing the cue. RULED 2026-10-08 (the texture pass, same ruling as lar:/ni: above): the '#' takes the anchor's own ink — the interior-separator law applied to the one separator this shared rule owns.

bearing.comment: The bearing arrow rides as an unnamed positional between two named ends. A bare `?` names nothing on its own — an end states itself as `from=?` or `to=?`, where the glyph reads as an ordinary value.

named-param.comment: The memetic standard writes key=value. TiddlyWiki reads `=` as the new-style separator (parseMacroParameterAsAttribute in core/modules/parsers/parseutils.js), which admits a filtered, indirect or macro value; a colon admits neither and demands a strict identifier so $:/foo cannot mis-parse. RULED 2026-10-08 (the operator's SECOND eyes-on pass): this rule is private to lar-uri (its only `#named-param` include), so `=` safely gains the value's own ink, `markup.other.value.lar.memetic-wikitext`, innermost — the interior-separator law applied to the one query separator this shared rule owns. The key's existing name stands unchanged; it was never named dishonest and no measured pair needed it moved.

sigil-marker.comment: THE MARKER EVERY SIGIL OPENS WITH. TiddlyWiki reads `<<~ set …>>` as a call on a variable spelled `~`, so the base names the `~` as the called name, and the dialect names it BESIDE that reading as the sigil's marker — closers included, `<<~/ahu>>`, which is why it is a marker and never an opener. The published punctuation name stands first and the keyword name second, so a theme ruling on the keyword decides its colour. It rides only an injection keyed on the base's own call-name scope: keyed on the root, a `(?<=<<)~` painted inside comments, raw fences and typed blocks, none of which builds a call.
sigil-marker.name: punctuation.definition.sigil.marker.memetic-wikitext keyword.control.sigil.marker.memetic-wikitext

sigil.comment: The verb a sigil says. TiddlyWiki reads `<<~ set …>>` as a call on a variable spelled `~`, so the verb binds as a POSITIONAL argument and the base paints it like any unquoted value — `set`, `oracle` and `lares` all read `string.unquoted`. The dialect names it BESIDE that reading rather than instead of it: the host builds a transclusion here and the base must keep saying so.

patterns.comment: An opening sigil, and a closing one, which TiddlyWiki reads as part of the variable name.

1.comment: THE MARK IS PART OF THE NAME THE HOST READS. TiddlyWiki takes the whole run after `<<` as ONE variable name, so `/ahu` names one closing sigil and a reader meets one object — and measured over 65 bundled themes, ALL 65 painted the mark apart from the verb while the mark itself read as ordinary prose in 36 of them. The sigil name rides second so a theme ruling on it decides, and the published punctuation name stands first for a reader who rules on that.
1.name: punctuation.definition.sigil.close.memetic-wikitext

ni-uri.comment: A block check names information by its DIGEST — `ni:///sha-256;<hash>`, RFC 6920 — and the house seals every carrier with one. The base grammar autolinks a CamelCase run, and measured, 21 of 22 hashes the house has written carry one, so every meme showed a spurious wikilink inside its own integrity stamp. Naming the whole URI takes the run before any inner rule reaches it. RULED 2026-10-06 (the punctuation-and-no-underline pass, same ruling as lar:): ni: names rather than fetches, so the enclosing family is colourless — `meta.uri.ni.memetic-wikitext`, measured 0/65 themes give it any style of its own; its ';' already read as plain punctuation and keeps doing so, and dropping the underline stops the OTHER separators (the ':' and the nested '/' runs) from inheriting a themed ancestor they have no business wearing. RULED 2026-10-08 (the texture pass, same ruling as lar: capture 2 and the authority above — see that rule's comment for the underline/texture reasoning): the scheme run `ni:///` reads as ONE colour — the ':' AND the three structural slashes nested in capture 3 stack the SAME scheme family capture 1 carries, since RFC 6920's `///` is scheme boilerplate (an empty authority), not a segment of its own. The ';' before the digest takes the digest's OWN ink instead, per the general interior-separator law (the ';' opens the digest, same as a path slash opens the path text beside it).
ni-uri.name: meta.uri.ni.memetic-wikitext

carrier.comment: A frame marker opens a block-check carrier rather than a sigil call, and TiddlyWiki reads it as the variable a call names — so the base offers a reader nothing to tell a carrier from any other call. What wikitext has no construct for, the dialect names. The base CAPTURES the marker as the variable a call names, so an R-priority injection reaches it nowhere — it rides with the arrow and the digest instead.
carrier.name: entity.name.function.carrier.memetic-wikitext

L:text.html.tiddlywiki5 variable.name.ca.comment: The sigil marker reads only inside a span the base already reads as a call's name, and nests beside that reading rather than replacing it.

R:text.html.tiddlywiki5 meta.variable.ca.comment: A sigil's verb reads only inside a call. TiddlyWiki builds a sigil as a call on a variable spelled `~`, so the verb stands wherever the base reads a call and nowhere else: text shaped like `<<~ set …>>` inside a comment, a raw fence or a typed block builds no call, and keyed on the root alone the verb painted there as a keyword. The selector demands the base's own call scope on the stack.

R:text.html.tiddlywiki5 - (meta.embedded.comment:
Carriers, addresses and bearings keep their reading everywhere the base grammar reads wikitext.

The base wraps everything after the pragma zone in a region of its own — a mode, not a construct — and a rule standing at this dialect’s top level cannot reach inside one.
An injection can: the base’s root scope stands on the stack wherever it reads, region or no region, so one selector reaches the whole file.
Naming the block contexts one at a time reached the three somebody listed.

FIX 2026-10-06 (a fence reads as the language its meta names): narrowed so the carrier/address/bearing family stops short of raw fences, fenced code, typed blocks and inline code spans, where the base grammar builds no call and the text underneath is held rather than addressed. A fence whose own info string names this dialect (`meta.embedded.block.memetic`, set by the base's own `mem`/`memetic`/`memetic-wikitext`/`text/memetic-wikitext+tiddlywiki` fence label) still carries `text.html.tiddlywiki5` and reads as an address, same as the top level — the second alternative restores exactly that one carrier, nothing wider.

L:text.html.tiddlywiki5 - (meta.embedded.comment:
A bearing arrow stands BETWEEN two named ends, inside a sigil where the base grammar's unquoted-value rule would take its dash and leave the angle to the parameters region — two tokens, neither named. An L-priority injection looks before that rule and keeps the arrow whole. It reaches only where this dialect stands, because a grammar's injections ride with the grammar.

FIX 2026-10-06 (same ruling as the R-priority memetic injection above): the ni: check, the bearing arrow and the carrier marker hold the same narrowing, for the same reason — a raw fence, fenced code, typed block or inline code span builds none of these, and the exception for a dialect-labelled fence restores them where the base's own dispatch already reads this tongue.
